text: tonic-clonic seizures as part of the syndrome of prima- ry generalised epilepsy, valproate is the drug of choice, al- though systematic reviews were unable to establish evi- dence for this.30,35 Topiramate is also considered a first choice in patients in whom the other older drugs are unsuitable or ineffective.16,22 More recently, valproate was found to be better tolerated than topiramate and more ef- fective than lamotrigine in generalised and unclassified epilepsy.37 Second-line drugs in UK guidelines are cloba- zam, levetiracetam, and oxcarbazepine, while other drugs that may be considered include acetazolamide, clon- azepam, phenobarbital, phenytoin, or primidone.16 Tia- gabine or vigabatrin should be avoided as they may wors- en the seizures.16 The drugs of choice for absence seizures are ethosux- imide, valproate, or, where these are unsuitable, lamotrig- ine,16,23,38 although the evidence base to support this use is weak.39 Second-choice drugs include clobazam, clon- azepam, and topiramate, but carbamazepine, gabapentin, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, tiagabine, and vigabatrin should be avoided as they may worsen seizures.16,38 Since absence seizures occur primarily in children the precau- tions concerning valproate hepatotoxicity apply. However, where absence seizures are associated with tonic-clonic seizures valproate is the drug of choice since it is effective in both conditions; valproate is also preferred for atypical absence seizures. Levetiracetam may be used as an alter- native for the syndrome of juvenile absence epilepsy.16 Valproate is normally the drug of choice for myoclonic seizures, including those associated with juvenile myo- clonic epilepsy.40,41 Lamotrigine may also be used in juve- nile myoclonic epilepsy,16,41 although some forms of myo- clonus may be exacerbated;16,40 topiramate may be con- sidered, particularly for severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy (in which stiripentol may also be effective), and second-line drugs also include clobazam and clonazepam, and adjunctive levetiracetam or piracetam.16 Zonisamide41 has also been used, as has ethosuximide. The classical antiepileptics may not be particularly effec- tive for atonic or tonic seizures, which are often associat- ed with specific epileptic syndromes or with cerebral dam- age or mental retardation.
